questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language - I speak Danish and English already, but I wanted to improve my German. And then I searched Google for the four possible German universities and I really liked how beautiful Heidelberg looked. Therefore, Heidelberg became my first priority, and Mannheim my second.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy in general.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had a lot of people ready to welcome us, which was great. The bad part was that it was in Heidelberg, not in Mannheim.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got it through Studierendenwerk, so it was pretty easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was a Studierendenwerk building, but not on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not a nice area, but the buildings and room in themselves were pretty, if a bit institution-like.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very applicable for my situation, since I only did clinical rotations.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I gave a copy of my passport and had filled out a paper, and submitted it to the study office. A couple of days later I got my student ID.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: People I could ask were there in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Only did clinical rotations.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have prepared everything for your arrival in Heidelberg, so you can walk over and registrer immediately! Especially if you live in Mannheim.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not applicable, only did clinical rotations.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not applicable, only did clinical rotations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Not applicable, only did clinical rotations.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Not applicable, only did clinical rotations. I would recommend the language course though.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a month travel card, since I had a language course in the beginning before the semester technically started, so my student ID wasnt valid for me to buy a semester ticket (which costs 180 euro and was going to cover the entire semester). The month card was 100 euros.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was unexpecting that I had to pay for my room for the entire semester, but I was also to sublet it for the last two and a half months.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of nice Erasmus Student Network activities in both Heidelberg and Mannheim, and also an opportunity to participate in sports with Uni Mannheim.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sightseeing tours, hiking, pub crawls, parties, christmas market tours and Octoberfest!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above, it was great! Wonderful sights in Heidelberg and the Odenwald area, trips to Strasbourg, Munich and along the Neckar.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Experience the local area and take some trips to go somewhere farther once in a while, if possible.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in ESN (Erasmus Student Network) activities, and make a Whatsapp Group with people you meet in the building.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: All of the physical paperwork, and the need for a German bank account, since my bank didn't allow SEPA transfers.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness to foreign students.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Go! It was great. Even if you are going to Mannheim, and you asked for Heidelberg, you will still have a very nice time.
2) Make sure to be open to making a lot of new friends continually. If you go to Mannheim and do the language course in Heidelberg first, you will need to get to know people once again in Mannheim, since you are in a new city now.
3) Speak German as much as possible to learn the language.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get a semesterticket when you get to Heidelberg, it makes travelling easier.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The other exchange students I got to know - just hanging in the evenings in people's rooms, and drinking tea or something. Alcohol wasn't needed unlike in Danish culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy was very difficult to deal with. Other than that I had a hard time with the change from being in Heidelberg during the language course and then being in Mannheim for clinical rotations. It was socially exhausting.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go abroad and enjoy being abroad. And go without another Dane to get the full international experience, or at least don't hang out with the Danish friend all the time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
